text:
amar: Thinking out loud — we need a new synth traffic generator focused on long-tail shaping (not just simple ramps). Goal: apples-to-apples kernel + batching comparisons across models. Want: deterministic seeds, KV-warmup control, and realistic burst semantics. Thoughts?

maria: Love it. Two immediate requirements: 1) model KV cache warmup vs cold-miss storms, 2) batch-size distribution reporting (not just avg). If bursts trigger many small batches we hide kernel perf. :exclamation:

liam: Agree. Also add reproducible burst schedules so we can compare across commits. Seeded bursts + stochastic background is ideal. Keep runs short-ish (10k-50k reqs) but with high variance.

jonathan: Proposal: three modes in the harness — replay (trace file), parametric (mix distributions), hybrid (replay bursts + parametric background). Example config snippet:```yamlmode: hybridbackground: poisson_lambda: 50 # rpsburst_profile: - type: pareto alpha: 1.5 scale: 0.05 duration_s: 2.0 schedule: random_seeds: [42, 99, 123]warmup: 5000 # requestsrecord_batch_composition: true```

maria: Nice. For the burst_profile, consider shot-noise (random pulse arrivals) so bursts can overlap. Also include correlated sequence-lengths: bursts often have longer prompts in our traces.

amar: Important: kernel selection changes depending on sequence length distribution and batch concurrency. The generator must tag requests with token_length and affinity so we can simulate kernel-switch patterns.

liam: Implementation detail: keep deterministic RNG seeds and export the exact timestamp stream and request-ids for each run: `requests.csv` with columns (ts, id, prompt_id, seq_len, seed). That lets us replay exactly.

perf-bot: profile-upload: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/1912345678 - artifacts: kernel_traces.pb, batch_hist.json, kv_trace.log

maria: Example quick-check metrics to compute after each run: [throughput_rps, p50/p90/p95/p99/p999, mean_batch_size, batch_size_histogram, kv_miss_rate, kernel_switch_count, gpu_util_pct, avg_latency_ms]. We should also capture 'stall_time' when runtime drains KV or switches kernels.

jonathan: For apples-to-apples: freeze model version + quantization flags + kernel selection flags in a manifest. Run against sequence lengths [32,128,512] and same prompt corpus. Compare with both `continuous_batching` on/off.

liam: Also log per-batch composition like `[{model_shard: a, seq_lens: [32,32,128], batch_size:3}, ...]` so we can correlate tail latencies with bad mixes.

amar: Perf regression hunting: if p99 jumps, check kv_miss timeline and kernel_switch_count. I've seen regressions caused by a new kernel that doesn't like interleaved short+long sequences — batch formation suffers.

maria: Small but useful addition — inject a tiny fraction of synthetic retries/timeouts to emulate client behavior and observe fallback policies.

liam: I'll prototype this harness tomorrow. Plan: 3 runs per config (seeds [42,99,123]), warmup 5k, measurement 20k, save artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/synth/1912345678/. expected quick sample output: `p99=214ms p999=482ms mean_batch=6.2 kv_miss=12% kernel_switches=37`

amar: Perfect. Also attach a short readme with instructions to reproduce and the manifest format. @maria can you add an eval prompt set (~200 prompts) that covers short/long/edge cases?

maria: On it. Will push prompt_set v1 to the repo and link in the run artifacts. :thumbsup:
